first_impression.reaction: Sophie sent me this because she's set on Hawaii, and Geoff's first question was 'is it even legal?'. The first paragraph answers that straight away, and in plain English, which I appreciated. I read it all on the iPad. It's calm, well ordered and leans on government websites, so I trust what it says about the paperwork. What it doesn't do is say a word about the people I'm worried about: my mother and Geoff's aunt on a very long flight, getting to a lawn above the sea, and what insurance we need. And I'd want to know that 'start a conversation' means a phone call with a real person.

journey.quote: There is no residency requirement, no US citizenship requirement and no blood test.
journey.reaction: Good. That settles Geoff's question in one line, and I can forward it to him as is.

journey.section: Can Australians marry legally in Hawaii?
journey.quote: The marriage licence is what permits the marriage to take place. The marriage certificate shows that a legal marriage has been performed.
journey.reaction: I would have mixed those two up. Thank you for spelling it out.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: [Smartraveller's United States advice](https://www.smartraveller.gov.au/destinations/americas/united-states-america) carries the overall advice level, "Exercise normal safety precautions", and lists an Australian Consulate-General in Honolulu for consular assistance.
journey.reaction: That's my 2am question, partly answered. There's an Australian consulate right there in Honolulu. Reassuring.

journey.section: Before you go: entry and documents
journey.quote: Keep both passports with you, not in the luggage you send ahead to the villa.
journey.reaction: Sensible, motherly advice. I'll be saying it too.

journey.section: Pick up your licence together, in person
journey.quote: Younger applicants need a certified copy of their birth certificate; check with the agent.
journey.reaction: Younger than what? The sentence before says the legal age is 18. I read it twice and still wasn't sure who this is for.

journey.section: Timing the appointment around your arrival
journey.quote: Leave a buffer before the rehearsal and the welcome dinner, and keep the appointment away from any day with an early inter-island flight.
journey.reaction: This is the practical planning I like. It tells me someone has actually thought about how the week runs.

journey.quote: If you book a local officiant, ask to see their current State of Hawaii performer licence before you pay a deposit.
journey.reaction: Finally, the word deposit. Good advice, but it's the only place money and protection come up. Who else are we paying deposits to over there, and are they safe?

journey.section: Getting your certificate ready for Australia
journey.quote: For peace of mind, a lawyer can confirm the certificate is valid in Australia.
journey.reaction: I like that it doesn't pretend to be the last word. Geoff will appreciate that.

journey.section: Permits for beach and outdoor ceremonies
journey.quote: A beach wedding on unencumbered State shoreline needs a right-of-entry permit through the Department of Land and Natural Resources' Wiki Permits system, and the permitted beach sites are listed by DLNR.
journey.reaction: 'Unencumbered State shoreline', 'right-of-entry', 'Wiki Permits'. Heavy going. I gather the beach needs a permit and the resort lawn may not, but I had to work for it. And a beach is no place for Mum's walking frame anyway.

journey.quote: Storms are infrequent, but they happen.
journey.reaction: Honest. But it stops short of the next thought: what happens to our money and the guests' flights if one comes through that week? That's an insurance question and the page doesn't touch it.

journey.quote: It suits a wedding weekend built around one resort and a long evening on the terrace.
journey.reaction: One resort, everyone in one place. That's what would work for the older relatives. I'd have liked the island section to say which is easiest for elderly guests: fewest connections, shortest transfers.

journey.quote: A Wedded Advisor plans your venue, travel, vendors and payments as one point of contact from start to finish, and confirms inclusions in writing before you commit.
journey.reaction: One person, payments included, everything in writing. That's what I want to hear when it's our money.

journey.section: Plan your Hawaii wedding with a Wedded Advisor
journey.quote: Your Wedded Advisor works in your time zone, quotes in AUD, and agrees the fee in writing before any work begins.
journey.reaction: AUD and the fee in writing. Good. But 'your time zone' is Melbourne, and the wedding is in Honolulu. Who do the children ring on the day if the shuttle doesn't turn up?

unanswered_questions: Who does the couple (or I) ring if something goes wrong in Hawaii outside Melbourne business hours? Is there anyone on the ground on the day? (deferred business detail)
Are our deposits protected if a Hawaii supplier, or Wedded Wonderland itself, fails? Whose name are the contracts in and in what currency?
What travel insurance should the couple and guests have for a Hawaii wedding, including cover for storms and for older guests' medical needs?
Which island and which kind of venue is easiest for elderly guests with limited mobility, and can step-free access to the ceremony spot be checked before booking?
Will Wedded Wonderland arrange transfers for guests from the airport to the resort, including for a guest with a walking frame? (deferred business detail)
Will Wedded Wonderland help with the licence paperwork and appointment booking, or is that entirely on the couple? (deferred business detail)
Is the first conversation a phone call with a real person, and can I join it as a parent paying part?
How is the fee charged and roughly what range, and do you receive commissions from Hawaii suppliers? (deferred business detail)
Have you planned real weddings in Hawaii I could look at, and how many? (deferred business detail)
Are there any extras or Wedded Privileges for couples who book with you? (deferred business detail)

turn_offs_found.quote: If you book a local officiant, ask to see their current State of Hawaii performer licence before you pay a deposit.
turn_offs_found.why: My turn-off is pages that skip contracts, deposits and who is responsible. This page is thorough on legal paperwork, but deposits appear once, for the officiant, and nothing is said about protecting money paid to overseas venues and suppliers or who is accountable if something falls over.

turn_offs_found.quote: A beach wedding on unencumbered State shoreline needs a right-of-entry permit through the Department of Land and Natural Resources' Wiki Permits system, and the permitted beach sites are listed by DLNR.
turn_offs_found.why: Government jargon in one long sentence. I don't mind detail, but I had to read it twice on the iPad to understand what it meant for us.

would_share_with: My husband, the intro and 'Getting your certificate ready for Australia', to settle whether the marriage counts at home, with my questions on deposits and insurance written underneath
My daughter, 'Timing the appointment around your arrival', so she doesn't book the licence appointment on the day of an inter-island flight

cta_reaction.quote: When you are ready, [start a conversation with Wedded Concierge](https://weddedwonderland.com/wonderland-concierge?utm_source=blog&utm_medium=content&utm_campaign=getting-married-in-hawaii&utm_content=closing).
cta_reaction.why: The page is careful and honest, and 'fee in writing before any work begins' and 'quotes in AUD' are what I want. But I'd talk to Geoff first, and I'd only go ahead if it's a phone call with a real person who can tell me how our deposits are protected, who looks after things on the day in Hawaii, and how they'd get my mother there comfortably.

top_3_changes: Add a short practical note for families: travel insurance for the couple and guests (including storm disruption and older travellers' medical cover) and checking step-free access at the ceremony spot, sourced (for example Smartraveller) or flagged for the business; otherwise point to the Advisor for it.
Fix 'Younger applicants need a certified copy of their birth certificate' so it is clear who it applies to, given the legal age of 18 stated just before.

Break the beach permit sentence into plain steps ('On a public beach you need a State permit. On a resort lawn, ask the venue.') and, if sourced, say in the closing that the first step is a phone call and a parent can join.

checks.check: Every journey point and turn-off has an exact quote from the draft
Journey types limited to gained_trust, lost_trust, confused, bored, excited, objection
Stayed in character as Margaret (funding parent): read top to bottom on iPad, focused on deposits, who is responsible, elderly guests, insurance and a phone call
No invented brand facts; on-the-ground support, deposit protection, transfers, paperwork help, fees, commissions, real weddings and Privileges placed in unanswered_questions
VERIFY markers and HTML comments (fact tags, image slots) ignored
Deferred business details listed as unanswered questions, not penalised or made must-fix

open_questions.question: Does the source pack hold anything on travel insurance or accessibility for older guests (for example Smartraveller insurance advice) that could support a short family-practicalities note? If not, flag rather than fill.

assumptions: Margaret arrived via a link from her daughter, reading on an iPad, as a parent contributing about half; relevance is 3 because the page is a legal how-to written to the couple, with nothing addressed to guests or family.
Elderly relatives travelling is a live concern for a destination wedding, so its absence was raised as an objection but kept low to medium severity given the article's legal focus.
The 3-minute budget covered the full article top to bottom, with the FAQ skimmed as it repeats the body.
